message.content:
QUALITY review (EFFICIENCY angle only) of the uncommitted F9 change set in /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim, a C++20 CLI driver `andes-sim`. F9 added `run --model hybrid` (orchestrate a QEMU1->vsim handoff for csr|pc|icount triggers).

Gather the diff:
- Modified: `cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim && git diff HEAD -- driver tests` (ignore ROADMAP.md).
- New files (git diff won't show untracked - Read them in full): driver/elf_syms.hpp, driver/elf_syms.cpp, driver/elf_syms_test.cpp, driver/hybrid.hpp, driver/hybrid.cpp, driver/hybrid_test.cpp, tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f9.sh

This is an EFFICIENCY review ONLY. Do NOT report correctness bugs or test gaps. Flag only wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O, copies where a move/reference would do, independent operations run sequentially that could overlap, work added to a startup/hot path.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT: this is a one-shot CLI driver, not a hot loop. Most "efficiency" in a CLI is irrelevant (it spawns multi-second qemu/vsim subprocesses). Be realistic: only flag things that are genuinely wasteful AND worth changing (e.g. reading a whole ELF file when a bounded read would do, an avoidable extra subprocess spawn, an unnecessary deep copy of a large buffer, engine discovery done when it could be skipped). Do NOT flag micro-optimizations (string concatenation, small-vector copies, a std::string by value) that won't matter next to a subprocess spawn.

Files to scrutinize:
- driver/elf_syms.cpp - it reads the entire ELF into memory (slurp). Is that justified or wasteful for a symtab lookup?
- driver/cmd_run.cpp run_hybrid() - order of discovery vs validation (does a cheap validation happen before expensive engine discovery? is discovery ever done redundantly?).
- driver/run_plan.cpp - any redundant rebuild of argvs/ctx.

Return a concise findings list, each with: file, approx line, one-line summary, concrete cost, the cheaper alternative, and whether it's actually worth fixing in a CLI. If there's nothing worth changing, say so plainly. Do not edit anything.

1	// ELF symbol resolution for pc-trigger boundaries (F9).
2	//
3	// pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs. Either boundary may be a
4	// "0x"-prefixed hex address (used verbatim) OR a symbol defined in the ELF
5	// (resolved against its .symtab). This decouples the switch points from the
6	// workload source -- any function can bound the ROI, with no planted markers.
7	//
8	// C++ port of tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc, reading the ELF .symtab directly via
9	// <elf.h> rather than shelling out to `nm`.
10	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
11	#define ANDES_SIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
12	
13	#include <string>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	// Resolve a pc-mode boundary to a bare hex address string (no "0x" prefix).
18	//   "0x<h>" / "0X<h>"  -> "<h>" verbatim (prefix stripped, digits unchanged)
19	//   <symbol>           -> the symbol's st_value as lowercase hex
20	// On any failure (undefined symbol, unreadable/!ELF file) returns "" and sets
21	// `err` to a message naming the boundary; on success leaves `err` empty.
22	std::string resolve_pc(const std::string& elf_path, const std::string& boundary,
23	                       std::string& err);
24	
25	}  // namespace andes_sim
26	
27	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP

19	// 10000 (qemu) / 5000 (vsim) -- matching the Python golden's argparse. The pc

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F9 contract: `run --model hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
3	# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the csr | pc | icount
4	# triggers. Three layers:
5	#
6	#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
7	#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution + icount defaults), the
8	#      trigger->argv mapping (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
9	#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
10	#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
11	#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
12	#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run csr/pc/icount through both
13	#      ./hsim (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
14	#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
15	#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
16	#
17	# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own csr markers as the boundaries (_start =
18	# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces csr's
19	# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
20	set -uo pipefail
21	
22	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
23	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
24	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
25	
26	BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
27	ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
28	CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
29	SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
30	ENG=verilator:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim resolves by default
31	
32	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
33	
34	# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
35	for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
36	  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
37	    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
38	done
39	echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"
40	
41	# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
42	# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
43	expect() {
44	  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
45	  local out rc
46	  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
47	  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
48	  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
49	}
50	expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid /no/such.elf
51	expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --model hybrid a.elf b.elf
52	expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
53	expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
54	  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
55	expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
56	expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
57	expect 2 'csr or pc'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount \
58	  --kanata /tmp/k "$SPIN"
59	expect 2 'requires --kanata' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr \
60	  --objdump /tmp/o "$ELF"
61	echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint/unknown trigger, kanata/objdump"
62	
63	# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
64	QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
65	SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
66	PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
67	if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim" ]; then
68	  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
69	  # line (golden csr/pc say "kernel_cycles", icount/andes say "window_cycles";
70	  # the number's position is identical).
71	  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
72	  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
73	    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
74	    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andes-sim produced no cycle number"
75	    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
76	    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
77	  }
78	
79	  # csr -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
80	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
81	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
82	  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[csr window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
83	    || fail "csr: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
84	  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --model hybrid --trigger csr ' \
85	    || fail "csr: missing PASS line: $AO"
86	  check_parity csr "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"
87	
88	  # csr on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
89	  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
90	  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
91	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
92	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
93	  check_parity csr-c "$GO" "$AO"
94	
95	  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
96	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode pc \
97	        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
98	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
99	        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
100	  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"
101	
102	  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
103	  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
104	  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
105	  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
106	  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"
107	
108	  # kanata ROI trace forwards onto the vsim leg and writes a non-empty file.
109	  KAN=$(mktemp); rm -f "$KAN"
110	  timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" \
111	    --kanata "$KAN" "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1
112	  [ -s "$KAN" ] || fail "kanata: trace file empty/missing after csr run"
113	  echo "[ok] kanata: csr run wrote a non-empty ROI trace ($(wc -l <"$KAN") lines)"
114	  rm -f "$KAN"
115	else
116	  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
117	fi
118	
119	ok "F9 run --model hybrid (csr|pc|icount)"
120

content.text:
Analysis complete. I've read the full diff, all six new files, and the supporting context (run_plan.cpp, cmd_run.cpp, engine_registry.cpp), and confirmed fixture sizes (5-56 KB) and that discover_engines() spawns a `--describe` subprocess per Verilator build.

## Verdict: nothing here is worth changing on efficiency grounds.

The startup path is already well-ordered: cheap validations (ELF existence, trigger/pc resolution, vsim-flag combos) run before the expensive `discover_engines()`, discovery is done exactly once and threaded into `run_plan` (no re-discovery), `run_plan` builds ctx/argvs once, and moves are used where they matter (`std::move(vsim_extras)`, `out.push_back(std::move(argv))`). The whole thing is dwarfed by the qemu + Verilator-vsim spawns that follow.

Three things I scrutinized and their realistic assessment:

### 1. `driver/elf_syms.cpp:23-31` - `slurp()` reads whole ELF with triple-buffering
- Summary: reads the entire file through `ostringstream`, then `ss.str()` (copy #1 into `s`), then `buf.assign` (copy #2 into the vector) - on top of the stream's own buffer, so ~3 in-memory copies of the file.
- Cost: for a 5-56 KB fixture, single-digit KB times three = microseconds; page-cached.
- Cheaper: `seekg`/`tellg`/`read` straight into the vector (one alloc, one copy). Or a bounded read (header + section headers + symtab/strtab only) instead of the whole file.
- Worth fixing? No. Reading the whole ELF is justified here - fixtures are tiny, a full slurp is simpler than seeking to four scattered sections, and it is gated to pc-trigger only (csr/icount never call `resolve_pc`). The triple-copy is real waste in the abstract but invisible next to a subprocess spawn.

### 2. `driver/hybrid.cpp:22-24` - `resolve_pc` called twice re-slurps + re-scans the symtab
- Summary: pc-trigger resolves `pc_start` and `pc_end` with two independent `resolve_pc` calls; when both are symbols, the ELF is slurped twice and the symtab scanned twice.
- Cost: 2x a ~50 KB read + 2x a few-hundred-symbol linear scan. Negligible, and only on the pc path with two symbol boundaries (a 0x boundary short-circuits before any read).
- Cheaper: slurp+parse once, do two name lookups.
- Worth fixing? No. Too contained and too cheap to matter.

### 3. `driver/cmd_run.cpp:136 vs 146` - `--mmap-size` parsed *after* `discover_engines()`
- Summary: every other cheap validation (trigger resolution, `vsim_extra_args`) is deliberately placed before discovery "so a bad combo fails fast", but the `parse_size(cli.mmap_size)` check sits *after* `discover_engines()`.
- Cost: a malformed `--mmap-size` (e.g. `64Q`) pays for a full `discover_engines()` - one `--describe` subprocess per Verilator build - before failing. Only on that error path; the success path is unaffected.
- Cheaper: move the `parse_size` block above `discover_engines()`, matching the surrounding fail-fast pattern.
- Worth fixing? Marginal. It is the one ordering inconsistency that contradicts the code's own stated principle, and the fix is a trivial block move, but it only bites a rare typo path. Take it or leave it.

No copies of large buffers across call boundaries, no redundant discovery, no sequential work that could overlap (the qemu->vsim legs are inherently ordered - vsim resumes from qemu's drain), and no work added to a genuine hot loop (this is a one-shot CLI).
